title: SynCare
description: UX design and research for SynCare, an AI health app that explains personal health records in plain language, designed over 10 weeks. All figures are design targets, not measured results.
hmw: design an emotionally supportive, human-centered digital health tool that integrates fragmented data sources into a coherent, personalized narrative empowering users with clarity, empathy, and insight while fostering psychological safety and positive health reflection?

heroImages.alt: SynCare AI app on a phone, with a person in the hero image

blocks.text: SynCare AI

Health records are hard to read, and patients work to make sense of them. Over 10 weeks at Patched Reality, I was a UX design and research collaborator on SynCare: an AI chat and personalized dashboard that explain records in plain, human-like language. Every figure below labeled “Design target” is a goal set during design, not a measured result.

items: Empower users through visibility and control
Enable early risk detection with AI-driven insights
Build trust through security and compliance (HIPAA readiness)

blocks.text: Seven patients, three clinicians and the literature

items: I audited existing EHR platforms and interviewed 7 patients and 3 clinicians about data access and coordination. The high-need use cases were chronic condition management, medication adherence and preventive screening.

I reviewed academic work on digital twins, personalization and context-aware design (Katsoulakis et al., 2024) and on AI ethics in health systems (Huang et al., 2022). It made trust and psychological safety core UX requirements, not only ethical ones.

I built low- to high-fidelity mobile prototypes: the conversational interface, a modular UI system for dashboards, summaries and alerts, a health timeline, AI-powered risk cards, a lab result normalizer and claims-integrated treatment suggestions.
I used the prototypes for stakeholder feedback and for usability evaluations of clarity, emotional support and personalization. This study reports no results from them.

blocks.text: Instant Clarity + Trust

SynCare AI aims for instant clarity and trust. A clean layout, strong brand presence and action-driven CTAs set the tone for onboarding, and guide people to value with minimal friction, which matters for a health app where trust, simplicity and control are critical.

cards.label: Time to action
cards.value: Design target: under 5 seconds to the first meaningful click

cards.label: Click-through rate
cards.value: Design target: 65-75% with strong CTA placement

cards.label: Bounce rate
cards.value: Design target: down by more than 20% when an intro carousel follows the welcome screen

cards.label: Cognitive load
cards.value: By design: only 3 UI elements (logo, tagline, CTA)

blocks.text: Converse with all your health apps

AI Chat turns static health data into natural, human-like dialogue. It lets users recall past appointments, track medication, and review fitness and vitals history. They can ask follow-up questions, get summarized reports and take quick actions, all in one thread.
Design rationale

The chat gives users clarity without requiring clinical literacy. Questions lower the friction, while structured information such as medication logs and appointment summaries stays within reach. It also connects past records to next actions.
AI Powered Vitals + Medication Dashboard
Design bet: AI-driven predictions earn more trust when paired with human-readable explanations.

The dashboard surfaces real-time health insights that are personalized, context-rich and actionable. Each screen adapts to its data sources, giving tailored summaries, timely medication reminders and AI-generated insights in a friendly, non-clinical interface.
Design rationale

The flow balances critical health data (blood glucose, vitals, meds) with human-centered messaging (“Hi, Lola!”). Microcopy explains why something is flagged, and AI tips and upcoming tasks suggest proactive care. The aim is less overwhelm, more trust and healthier habits.

cards.label: Daily check-in time
cards.value: Design target: under 60 seconds for a complete overview

cards.label: Info density
cards.value: By design: 3 key data blocks per scroll, with low visual noise

cards.label: CTA clarity
cards.value: By design: one primary interaction path per panel

blocks.text: A Deep dive into Vitals

The vitals screen gives a quick, reassuring overview of key health stats, with contextual support when something is off. When blood glucose is high, the UI responds with calm messaging and clear, actionable tips, so users feel informed rather than alarmed. A consistent card structure supports habit formation and quick scanning.
Design rationale

It combines medical accuracy with emotional support, using friendly language and visual clarity to encourage positive behavior. The experience is personalized and educational without being overwhelming.

cards.label: Behavioral tips
cards.value: Design target: +35% uptake when paired with elevated readings

cards.label: App abandonment
cards.value: Design target: more than 25% lower after alert events

blocks.text: Your personal AI fitness coach

The fitness page gives daily movement insights, hydration levels and exercise logs, paired with personalized AI recommendations. Step count, distance, calories and yoga time appear alongside motivational tips and daily notes.
Design rationale

Encouraging feedback reinforces positive behavior, and key activity metrics stay glanceable. User-written daily notes support self-reflection and accountability, closing the loop between awareness and action.

cards.label: Trust signals
cards.value: Design intent: a human-like tone and accurate memory to build trust and retention

cards.label: Engagement rate
cards.value: Design target: +50% vs a standard record view

cards.label: Less confusion
cards.value: Design target: more than 45% less confusion about prescriptions among patients

blocks.text: Three calls that shaped SynCare

cards.label: Trust as a requirement
cards.value: Chose to treat trust and psychological safety as core design requirements, because the literature framed them as essential UX considerations, not just ethical ones.

cards.label: Chat with structure
cards.value: Chose a conversational interface that keeps structured information such as medication logs and appointment summaries within reach, because users need clarity without clinical literacy.

cards.label: Calm explanations
cards.value: Chose calm messaging and microcopy that says why something is flagged, because users should feel informed rather than alarmed.

blocks.text: Limits

items: Every figure labeled “Design target” was a goal I set during design. None was measured, and this study reports no results from the usability evaluations.
Goals such as HIPAA readiness describe the direction of the design. They are not a claim of compliance.
I worked on this as a UX design and research collaborator for 10 weeks, so the study shows the research and the design, not the product’s outcomes.
